title: Revealing the Quantum Signature of Gravity via Gravitational Waves
abstract: Can propagating gravitational waves serve as operational probes of the quantum nature of gravity? We address this question by developing a unified theoretical framework that combines spacetime geometry, quantum information, and gravitational-wave physics. Starting from the geodesic deviation equation in linearized General Relativity, we derive the effective detector Hamiltonian directly from spacetime geometry and construct the complete quantum dynamics for detector subsystems interacting with both classical and quantized propagating gravitational-wave fields. This unified formulation enables a direct comparison between classical and quantum descriptions of gravitational radiation within the same physical framework. We demonstrate that classical gravitational-wave backgrounds can induce mixedness in the detector state but cannot generate genuine quantum correlations between the detector subsystems. In contrast, quantized gravitational waves coherently mediate gravity-induced entanglement, quantum coherence, quantum memory, and nonclassical correlations, providing clear operational signatures of the quantum nature of propagating gravitational radiation. We further discuss how mesoscopic quantum mechanical oscillators offer a promising route towards experimentally probing these effects. Our results establish a geometric and quantum-information-based framework for exploring quantum gravity through propagating gravitational waves.
summary: This work establishes a quantum information-based framework to test quantum gravity using gravitational waves. By analyzing the quantum dynamics of coupled detectors, the authors show that only quantized gravitational fields can generate genuine entanglement between detectors. This provides a clear, operational signature distinguishing quantum gravity effects from classical predictions.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether propagating gravitational waves can serve as operational probes to detect the quantum nature of gravity, moving beyond classical measurements of spacetime perturbations.
main_result: Quantized gravitational waves can coherently mediate genuine entanglement between two spatially separated detectors, a signature that cannot be generated by classical stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds.
method: The authors develop a unified theoretical framework by deriving the effective detector Hamiltonian from the geodesic deviation equation and constructing the full quantum dynamics for the detector subsystems.
model_or_system: The model involves localized quantum oscillators (detectors) coupled to a propagating gravitational-wave field, analyzed within the weak-field regime of linearized General Relativity.
key_observables: Entanglement negativity, quantum coherence, quantum memory, and the comparison between detector mixedness (classical) versus entanglement (quantum).
important_parameters: The analysis relies on the weak-field, perturbative, and single-mode approximations.
main_assumptions: The study is an operational analysis of propagating radiation and does not constitute a complete theory of quantum gravity.
paper_structure: The paper is structured around establishing the quantum information framework, deriving the Hamiltonian, formulating the dynamics, and finally comparing the entanglement generated by classical versus quantized fields.
why_interesting: The core mechanism—using entanglement as a diagnostic tool to distinguish quantum from classical field interactions—is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum optics, as it provides a concrete, measurable quantum signature.
